name: Chuck Schumer
role: U.S. senator from New York (1999-present); Senate Democratic leader (2017-present), majority leader 2021-2025
summary: Mainstream liberal Democrat who favors abortion rights, gun control, a higher minimum wage, taxes on the wealthy, union rights, student debt cancellation, cannabis legalization, same-sex marriage and large public investment in clean energy and technology. He supports Israel's statehood and a negotiated two-state solution, NATO and aid to Ukraine, comprehensive immigration reform alongside border security, and the death penalty for terrorism. His record on finance and trade is more mixed than his rhetoric.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He voted for the 1999 resolution authorizing American forces to conduct air operations with NATO and for the 2002 authorization to use United States armed forces against Iraq.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: He voted for the American Taxpayer Relief Act in 2013, which retained the federal individual income tax and restored a higher rate for the top bracket.

abolish-ip.rationale: He voted in 2011 for the America Invents Act, which amended and maintained the federal patent system.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: No position on this specific claim was established by the sources reviewed.

abortion-legal.rationale: He voted in 2022 to advance the Women’s Health Protection Act, which would have protected abortion access before viability and under specified health circumstances after viability.

anonymous-payments.rationale: His 2011 letter cited Bitcoin’s perceived untraceability when asking federal authorities to shut down Silk Road for illegal drug sales. The requested action concerned the marketplace and left lawful anonymous payments unaddressed.

automation-leaves-most-without-work.rationale: No position on this specific claim was established by the sources reviewed.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: No position on this specific claim was established by the sources reviewed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He voted for the 1999 Gramm–Leach–Bliley conference report allowing broader affiliations among banks, securities firms and insurers, and for stricter bank oversight under Dodd–Frank in 2010. In 2018 he voted against easing those standards.

rehabilitation.rationale: His 2018 vote for the First Step Act supported rehabilitation programs and earned-time credits. The bill did not set rehabilitation above punishment as the primary purpose of prisons.
